query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: In compositionally complex high-entropy alloys, brittle behavior emerges not primarily from intergranular segregation or large-scale precipitation as in conventional alloys, but from processing-induced nanoscale microstructural instabilities that act as local stress concentrators. In particular, selective laser melting (SLM) conditions may introduce subtle heterogeneities—such as localized dislocation pile-ups or nano-scale inclusions near grain boundaries—that lower hot ductility under high-temperature and rapid loading conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: An initially single-phase high-entropy alloy with a homogeneous elemental distribution and minimal conventional grain-boundary precipitates.
generation.intervention: A controlled variation in processing conditions comparing SLM-processed HEAs with conventionally processed (thermomechanically treated) HEAs, while systematically varying cooling rates and build parameters.
generation.conditions: Mechanical testing under high-temperature conditions and rapid loading rates representative of demanding engineering service environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Localized nanoscale heterogeneities (e.g., dislocation pile-ups or nano-scale inclusions) emerging at or near grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Subtle variations in SLM processing promote microstructural defects that concentrate stress and facilitate premature crack initiation. These nanoscale defects weaken the material’s ability to dissipate energy, leading to a drop in ductility and an emergent brittle failure mode distinct from the conventional mechanisms (grain-boundary segregation and intermetallic precipitation).
generation.predicted_outcome: SLM-processed HEAs will exhibit a significant drop in hot ductility and an increased incidence of brittle fracture under high-temperature and rapid loading conditions compared to conventionally processed HEAs, which should maintain a more uniform microstructure and higher toughness.
generation.baseline: Conventionally processed HEA with a uniform, nearly defect-free microstructure exhibiting robust toughness under similar service conditions.
generation.boundary: The effect is expected to be pronounced under high-temperature service and rapid loading conditions; outside these regimes, the differences between processing routes may be less appreciable.
generation.uncertainty: There remains uncertainty regarding the precise nature, size, and spatial distribution of the nanoscale heterogeneities, and the relative contribution of these defects versus any minor segregation effects that may also be present.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of HEA samples: one produced via SLM under varied cooling and laser parameters, and the other produced by conventional thermomechanical processing. Subject both sets to in-situ high-temperature mechanical testing with rapid loading rates while monitoring the microstructural evolution with high-resolution electron microscopy.
measurements: Quantitative analysis of hot ductility (e.g., strain to failure) and toughness.
In-situ observation of dislocation structures and micro-crack initiation sites.
High-resolution chemical and structural mapping near grain boundaries.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If SLM-processed samples do not show a statistically significant increase in nanoscale heterogeneities and brittle fracture events, and if their high-temperature ductility is comparable to that of conventionally processed samples, then the hypothesis that processing-induced nanoscale defects are responsible for emergent brittleness in HEAs is falsified.
